dates: Four disjoint UTC weeks from 2026-10-22 through 2026-11-18. Retrospective first-submission dates; text and category versions are those supplied at retrieval.
intake: Fetch the union of all 16 archive tags, including cross-listings. Each terminal arXiv request reconciles versionless unique IDs with totalResults. Split date ranges above 2,000, and retry smaller date ranges after HTTP 429. Every admitted record has a title, abstract and first-submission date inside the window. A paper can be counted by more than one archive but only once per arm.

arm_definitions.four: The four public archive tags and four primary-category labels.
arm_definitions.six: Also admit astro-ph.SR and astro-ph.GA and use their two labels.
arm_definitions.sixteen: Sixteen admitted archives and twelve named primary labels.
arm_definitions.sixteen_with_four_labels: Same works and clusters as sixteen, retaining the four original primary labels.

controlled_rank: For each week sort unique arXiv IDs, embed each title + newline + abstract once with allenai/specter2_base, then subset the vectors and run pipeline.cluster.cluster_items. Use complete linkage, cosine distance 0.10 and minimum group size three. Each arm uses the source primary label or other-physics for a cross-listing with an outside primary. Use the majority category with alphabetical tie-breaks and the production keyword_slug, signals_for, score_topics and rank functions with an empty history, category floor one, cap eight and top 40. This isolates source and category sensitivity before editorial selection. The live service uses learned relevance/categories, first-seen dates and topic history. The broader hosted pilot screens cluster cohesion.
topic_comparison: Exact topic matches require identical supporting ID sets in the top ten lists. Partial matching considers descending Jaccard, then rank, accepting a one-to-one match at intersection/union of at least 0.5. Counts for new/cross-listed archives overlap.

independent_index.reference: INSPIRE literature index (its records also draw on arXiv). Query each archive for earliest_date in the inclusive UTC window. Enumerate every result and deduplicate across categories by arXiv identifier. A match requires an arXiv versionless identifier, its first-submission date in the same week, and at least one of its queried arXiv categories. Neither source represents journal-only works by this definition.

native_listing_sample.method: On each official November monthly listing take the primary entries, sort by SHA-256 of the versionless ID, then select the first four whose separate v1 abstract page gives a first-submission date within the 28-day window. The sampling frame is the November listing as observed on November 20, not all October submissions. Check membership, date and primary category against the intake.

limits: This trial has no journal-only intake. Atomic and molecular physics, physics instrumentation, and much of condensed matter remain outside these 16 archive tags. Neither the source sensitivity calculation nor 28-day group counts establish editorial readiness or daily operating cost.

long_window_reading.selection: Read examples 1, 5 and 10 of the ten deterministically recorded 28-day groups containing at least one newly grouped paper. These examples precede editorial screening and are not a rate estimate.

cases.finding: Two papers study discrete time crystals. An Otto cycle, a quench of a spin chain and channel dynamics in a different qubit do not supply a third paper on either time-crystal stability or its proposed witness.

The papers calculate black-hole quasinormal frequencies, mode behavior or stability in specified backgrounds. The longer window recovers related theoretical work on a common observable. Some papers also address emission or censorship; preserve the individual spacetime and mode assumptions in any synthesis.

One paper develops vibrational imaging at interfaces, another compares melanin with pump–probe microscopy, and the third surveys pathology imaging. The three share an imaging modality family but no single measurement target.
